title: Student Engagement in Business Schools: Strategies to Build Stronger Communities
summary: Student engagement in business schools goes beyond event attendance. Discover four strategies from Haas, Questrom, and ESCP to build stronger communities.
body_markdown:
Student engagement plays a distinctive role in the business school experience. It helps students develop leadership skills, expand professional networks, and build relationships that can support them throughout their careers.


Yet business schools face specific challenges in encouraging participation. Students must balance demanding schedules with internships, job searches, and career development. How can institutions encourage participation, support student development, and build communities that remain valuable beyond graduation?


In this post, we look at how top business schools foster student engagement, drawing on insights from the University of California, Berkeley’s Haas School of Business, Boston University’s Questrom School of Business, and ECSP Business School.


## 4 Top Strategies for Improving Student Engagement in Business Schools


### 1. Rethink Student Engagement Beyond Attendance


Attendance is an easy starting point for measuring student engagement, but headcount alone doesn’t reveal what students gain from participating or how much they contribute to their communities.


#### Consider ownership, not just attendance


For Joy Bianchi, Associate Director of Student Life and Leadership Development for the full-time Master of Business Administration (MBA) program office at the University of California, Berkeley’s Haas School of Business,


**engagement increasingly means looking at student ownership** .


> *“I’m starting to think about it more in terms of ownership. Not only are students attending events, but are they actually taking ownership of the events?”*


At Haas,


[student organizations](https://www.readyeducation.com/campusgroups/student-organization-management-software-campus-groups/) are a primary driver of engagement. Bianchi advises and serves as a liaison to more than 50 clubs, and she looks at:


- How many students remain active.


- How many students pursue leadership roles.


- How much programming students organize on their own.


Running a club or organizing a conference requires planning, coordination,


[communication](https://www.readyeducation.com/solutions/student-communication/) , and collaboration.


#### Focus on what participation leads to


Joe Grande, Associate Director of MBA Community Engagement at Boston University’s Questrom School of Business, brings a similar focus to engagement. His work with graduate business students has shifted his perspective beyond traditional activity attendance.


For these students,


**participation is about more than showing up** . It can mean meeting the right people, discovering relevant resources, or finding opportunities that support their goals. That matters at business schools, where involvement is a chance to practice leadership, build professional relationships, and explore career paths before entering the workplace.


[Co-curricular transcripts](https://www.readyeducation.com/articles/co-curricular-transcripts-an-important-compass-of-college-life/) can help students recognize and document the skills they develop along the way.


### 2. Connect Community Engagement With Career Development


Business students often evaluate extracurricular activities through a career-focused lens, and understanding that mindset helps schools explain why engagement matters. As Bianchi puts it:


> *“Business students tend to be really ROI-driven and transactional, even though they also need community.* ”


Students may prioritize networking events, employer presentations, and activities that have a clear connection to their job searches, so they can overlook community


[events](https://www.readyeducation.com/articles/event-management-and-engagement-made-easy-with-campusgroups/) whose value is less immediately apparent. Business schools can make that value visible by pairing social events with opportunities to access:


- Relevant


[campus resources](https://www.readyeducation.com/campusgroups/student-services-software/) .


- Job postings.


- Mentoring.


- Other career-focused activities.


These pairings help students see how involvement contributes to their professional development while building relationships with peers and the wider business school community. The challenge is making these opportunities easy to find, and


[clear communication](https://www.readyeducation.com/articles/how-to-improve-your-business-schools-student-communications/) is a big part of that. When students can easily discover activities and understand their value, they have more ways to participate.


### 3. Create a Connected Experience Across Programs and Campuses


Some business schools serve students across multiple programs, locations, and communities. Keeping communication and access to opportunities consistent is hard when each team relies on different, disconnected tools.


#### The Challenge


ESCP Business School offers an example of how institutions can connect these communities. With campuses across six countries, ESCP needed to bring together a diverse student population while accommodating local needs.


#### ESCP’s Approach


The


[ESCP CampusLife platform](https://www.readyeducation.com/success-story/escp-business-school/) , powered by CampusGroups, brings events, student societies, resources, and


[communication](https://www.readyeducation.com/campusgroups/student-communication-platform/) together in one shared environment. Students can discover opportunities across campuses, while local teams retain the flexibility to tailor content and workflows to their needs.


#### The Results


- All 193 societies use ESCP CampusLife to


[manage events](https://www.readyeducation.com/campusgroups/streamline-university-event-management-campusgroups/) and group activities.


- Platform usage more than doubled in one year.


- The platform now has more than 20,700 active users across Europe.


Agnese Macerini, Turin Campus Student Affairs Coordinator for Student Experience at ESCP, describes the benefit to students:


> “ESCP CampusLife gives them one place to find everything.”


For schools with multiple programs or international campuses, that kind of connected experience can create a more consistent community experience without losing local flexibility.


### 4. Support Students from Orientation through Alumni


Building a strong business school community means supporting students from the moment they’re admitted through graduation and into their careers. Starting early helps admitted students make connections and feel confident about getting involved. Introduce them to clubs, let them preview the events coming up in the first weeks, and give new students chances to mingle during


[orientation](https://www.readyeducation.com/articles/fun-college-orientation-ideas/) .


The same continuity pays off after graduation. Alumni connections support networking, career development, mentorship, and a lasting relationship with the school. A student engagement platform can bring these opportunities together in one place. Because alumni already know the platform from their time as students, it’s a


**natural extension of their campus experience.** Current students benefit too, since alumni can share professional insights, offer mentorship, and help students build connections.


### What should a business school look for in a student engagement platform?


A platform that carries students from orientation to alumni should offer:


- **One place for everything:** Clubs, events, mentoring, job postings, and alumni access that live together, so students don’t have to switch between tools.


- **Mobile access:** Students should have the ability to find and join clubs, register for events, and connect with peers from any device.


- **Flexible structure:** Schools should have the ability to tailor content to each program or campus.


- [Integrations with your existing systems](https://www.readyeducation.com/campusgroups/integrations/) **:** Connections to the tools you already use, such as your student information system and single sign-on.


- [Intelligent analytics and reporting](https://www.readyeducation.com/campusgroups/data-intelligence/) **:** Staff should be able to understand how participation and leadership help drive positive outcomes for students.

## Student Engagement in Business Schools: FAQs


### When should business schools start encouraging engagement among new students?


Before classes start. Introduce admitted students to clubs, send them a preview of events that will take place early in the year, and give new students chances to connect during orientation, so they arrive knowing people and feeling confident about getting involved.


### How can student engagement data drive decision-making?


Engagement shows which clubs and events draw the most students, which student populations need more support, and where budget and staff members’ time will have the greatest effect.
